answer: Picture a harbor behind a velvet rope, where every berth sits behind a reef of escrowed bonds: a newcomer posts a deposit scaled to the square of berths already occupied, refundable only after long uninterrupted tenure. A fleet of k clones thus locks roughly k-cubed divided by three base stakes, none of it poolable, since each refund path is keyed to one identity's own record. Every marginal berth costs more than the last, so the reef deepens faster than a farm can grow, while honest incumbents keep their collateral intact.
